title: Verify Temper Windows dependency modes after product relocation
description: Temper was structurally relocated into its standalone swift-universal product repository before compatibility repair. Manifest parsing and dependency resolution reached the build stage, but the controlled swift-argument-parser checkout conflicts with temper-swift's remote identity and its GenerateDoccReference plugin does not compile under the current Windows Swift 6.4 toolchain.

historicalContent.expectedBehavior: Temper builds and tests on Windows from its canonical product repository in both default remote-dependency mode and an explicitly selected compatible local-dependency mode.
currentEvidence: swift package dump-package succeeded from private/product-lines/temper.
SwiftPM resolved the temper-swift dependency from its existing standalone checkout.
The controlled swift-argument-parser checkout produced a duplicate package-identity warning against temper-swift's remote dependency.
GenerateDoccReference.swift failed because GeneratePlugin was unavailable and the @main type had no recognized main entry point under Swift 6.4 on Windows.
acceptanceCriteria: Run swift build and swift test successfully from the canonical Temper repository on Windows using the default dependency mode.
Define one compatible controlled-local dependency graph without duplicate swift-argument-parser identities.
Repair or version-gate the controlled GenerateDoccReference plugin for the supported Windows Swift toolchain.
Save concise build and test evidence in the Temper product Kura space.
historicalContent.scopeBoundary: Complete the repository relocation independently; perform dependency and toolchain compatibility changes only in the canonical Temper repository.
